item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
When this SCP holds a human form, like for example the Egyptian Pharaoh it is essentially a normal human (bedsides when its producing art, in that case, he becomes unkillable and immovable) so if he gets shot in the head he will die, his body will plummet to the ground and will stay there rotting, eventually, the rotting corpse will begin to shapeshift into the next form that being the priest-ish looking medieval painter, when it cycles back around to the Egyptian Pharaoh he will be alive again like nothing happened, now that you mentioned I think I did not word that concept the best way.

And the danger I've imagined for at least one of the "masterpieces" is being so incredibly good anyone who looks at will see literally everything in life as a disappointment since nothing can reach that level of greatness anymore, and the person will kill themselves, maybe if an abstract masterpiece is created anyone who looks at it will lose their perception of reality with literally everything turning into random incompressible shapes the subject who viewed the painting being doomed to never being able to put sounds, sights and feeling into something remotely understandable, I still have some brainstorming to do but thanks for the feedback!

item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded: I really like the idea here, I think it's pretty unique, but I'm a little confused with how the immortality and multiple identities work. You say the scp is impossible to kill, but can die. Does this mean that it is impervious to any weapons, but can die from old age or disease? and in that case, does it just live a normal human life span until dying and being reincarnated as one of the 10 different forms? If that is how it works, I think a cool idea to add would be that within each of its life spans, it, as you describe, goes from asking for basic supplies, to more extreme mediums, and at the end of each life span it attempts to do something SUPER dangerous and the foundation has to do something to stop it each time. I'm not sure how dangerous art could be lol, but maybe you could think of something.

item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
All of the instances are kind of the same entity and not the same entity at the same time.
They all have certain memories which are shared between all instances, but none of the instances know about each other and their experiences, the scientist's current hypothesis is that it is an entity who got way too much into character for these caricatures of people, kind of dissociating and losing its sense of self, the only evidence is that they all have certain key memories that are shared between them all, so, for now, it's quite the stretch.

Thanks for the feedback!

item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
This concept is very cool indeed, it is still a bit bare but definitely has potential. I like how it escalates from simple requests to making carving tools out pf the bones of a person ir had just killed.

I have a question, though. All the instances are the same being or is it a collective of beings? The description was a bit unclear to me. If they are a group it could be interesting to have them competing to see who creates the masterpiece first. You can even hint at what kind of thing it is and how the Foundation keeps them from achieving it (maybe their masterpiece can destroy the world so they think sacrificing some D-class to keep it from being made is a viable option)

I hope this can be useful. Good luck and if you wish to debate further I am here :)

item.title: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is an unidentified being that has shown itself quite fascinated by human art, it regularly shape-shifts between 10 forms, each representing an art movement in history, these forms vary from a stoic Egyptian Pharaoh to a very surreal blob of energy that is a visual representation of the concept of "Abstract" the thing all of these instances share in common is the desire to produce a masterpiece, any damage to their art can and will be retaliated.

This SCP requests increasingly more and higher quality art supplies to make its own art, it went from being satisfied with paper and crayons to demanding the amount of paint equivalent of what would be needed to paint the Sistine Chapple

Idea derived from a suggestion from user Kingyo: once an instance of the SCP makes a "masterpiece" the painting will induce several anomalous effects on the viewer such as an urge to kill themselves since everything after seeing such a great painting would be a letdown

This SCP wants to create art, not just art, the greatest piece of art the world has ever laid their eyes on, and it will keep trying, and trying, if it's art supplies are not provided quickly it will find a suitable replacement, by any means necessary, for example shaping a human bone enough to make it able to carve a hieroglyph on a wall.

Central Narrative: A foundation scientist will try to maintain a concise conversation with this SCP between it's constantly changing identities, even though every change apparently induces amnesia in all the forms of this SCP.

The scientist will find that this SCP has seen a lot, as it tends to act like a fanboy when certain artists are name-dropped and give huge exposition dumps to its own experiences.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that an SCP whose abilities are directly connected with art history is quite a fascinating idea, and something that I least think has not been done in this way.

Additional Notes: I think it's important to clarify some things about this SCP

1.All of its 10 form have no knowledge of each other
2. They all request different Art Supplies
3. They all will turn any matter around them into a suitable replacement.
